clue.text: It'll be seven, if you don't get a shift on!

definitions.text: It'll be seven, if you don't get a shift on!

parts.words: It'll be seven, if you don't get a shift on!
parts.note: on a standard keyboard the symbol for 'and' shares the 7 key and needs the shift key held down; without shift you just type the figure seven

explanation.surface: Someone is warned they will be late, arriving at seven, unless they hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a shift on' is British slang for hurry up, but here it means pressing the shift key on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol & sits on the 7 key of a typewriter or computer keyboard and is reached with shift.

clue.text: Jelly and some pistachio ice cream for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so each of these words gives only its first letter

explanation.surface: A dessert menu offers jelly alongside some pistachio ice cream to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat or fish stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Brunch this term offered in case

definitions.meaning: brunch is a blend word, made from breakfast and lunch run together, which is what this kind of word is called
a large travelling bag that opens into two halves

explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll coined the word for a blend like brunch, borrowing the name of a hinged leather suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a blended coinage and an old-fashioned two-compartment suitcase.

clue.text: Rambling red rose makes a screen

indicators.note: a rambling rose grows untidily in all directions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A climbing red rose grows thick enough to hide something from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' looks like a description of the rose, a rambler being a climbing variety, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or partition behind a church altar.

clue.text: One prefers squash to snakebite?

parts.note: reads as a drinker choosing a soft fruit drink over cider and lager, but describes a large snake that kills by crushing rather than by a venomous bite

explanation.surface: Someone at the bar opts for a soft drink rather than a cider-and-lager mix.
explanation.walkthrough: Squash is a British fruit cordial and snakebite a pub drink of lager and cider; the snake in question constricts its prey instead of biting it with venom.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaconda is a South American constrictor that squeezes its prey to death rather than poisoning it.

clue.text: Mizzle makes you wet touring middle of Lake Como

indicators.note: something touring goes round, so the word for wet encloses the other piece

parts.note: damp means slightly wet

indicators.note: the central letters of the phrase Lake Como are taken

explanation.surface: A drizzly day soaks someone on a trip round Lake Como.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mizzle' looks like the dialect word for drizzle, which fits the wet surface, but here it is old slang for running off. 'middle of' takes the two central letters of the lake's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: To mizzle is old slang for to make off or disappear, the same as to leave hurriedly.

clue.text: Expert setter returned for introduction

parts.note: a pro is an expert or professional

indicators.note: returned means the word for the setter is read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so setter gives me

explanation.surface: A skilled puzzle compiler comes back to write an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a preface or preamble at the start of a book or speech.

clue.text: Voracious eater managed to tuck into most of pie and ham

indicators.note: to tuck into is to go inside, so this piece is placed within the others
each of the two words loses its last letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
taken as written before trimming
to run something is to manage it, so managed gives ran

explanation.surface: A hungry person manages to dig into most of the pie and ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' applies to both foods at once, each losing its final letter; 'to tuck into' then puts the word for managed between the two shortened words.
explanation.definitionFit: The piranha is a sharp-toothed South American fish famous for its ferocious feeding.

clue.text: Upset half wading bird's eggs

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top
only half of the bird's name is kept, the latter three letters being dropped

parts.note: the avocet is a long-legged wading bird with an upturned bill

explanation.surface: Someone disturbs a wading bird's clutch of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of AVOCET is AVO; 'Upset' turns it over to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural of ovum, meaning egg cells or eggs.

clue.text: Ready made here, to go on lip? It goes on joint

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece going on another sits on top of it, so it comes first

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, and the place where money is made is a mint
lip means cheeky talk, which is also sauce

explanation.surface: A kitchen-made condiment is about to be dabbed on someone's lip, and it goes well on a roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for cash, as in 'the readies'. The British serve this with roast lamb, the 'joint' of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This green herb sauce is the traditional accompaniment to a roast joint of lamb.

clue.text: He cuts half of pack with King and Queen

indicators.note: only the front half of the word pack is used

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: Someone takes half a deck of cards with the king and queen in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' and 'pack' suggest a card game, but the definition is someone who pares or peels.
explanation.definitionFit: A parer is someone or something that trims or pares, as in peeling fruit.

clue.text: Find out how sectarian may be converted

indicators.note: converting something changes its form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a narrow-minded zealot might be won over to another faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suits the religious surface of 'sectarian', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to discover or establish something for certain.

clue.text: Broadcast scene from Monday's play?

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so these letters are spread and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A radio station airs a scene from the play scheduled for Monday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio, but it signals the anagram of SCENE FROM MONDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy of manners is a genre of play satirising the behaviour of fashionable society.

clue.text: Shocking results if he gets it wrong

definitions.text: Shocking results if he gets it wrong

parts.words: Shocking results if he gets it wrong
parts.note: the shock here is a literal electric shock, the risk for a tradesman who wires something badly

explanation.surface: A warning that a careless person's mistake will have scandalous consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrician installs wiring, and a wiring mistake can give someone an electric shock.

clue.text: Piece of jewellery left, say, on expensive sort of seat

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery
left is an example of a side, the 'say' marking it as one instance

explanation.surface: A woman wears jewellery and sits on the left in a pricey seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringside seat is right beside a boxing ring and is among the most costly places.

clue.text: Artist with crayon visits old city storyteller

indicators.note: the artist and his crayon go to the city, so it follows them

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
conte is a hard crayon of graphite and clay, named after its inventor
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A painter with a drawing stick goes to an ancient city and tells tales of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes and stories.

clue.text: Entrance to a university named for Black Forest?

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A college entrance is named after a forest region of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black Forest' reads as the German region, but the question mark signals an example: a Black Forest is a chocolate and cherry cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Forest is a famous kind of rich chocolate cake, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Did damage, gripping expensive French lampholder

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside, so the word for damage wraps round the French word

parts.note: tore means ripped, which is doing damage
cher is the French word for expensive

explanation.surface: Someone vandalised a costly French lamp stand while holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: A torchere is a tall ornamental stand for holding a lamp or candelabrum.

clue.text: Indian party lacking skill, causing horror

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written before the removal
art means skill

explanation.surface: A clumsy party of Native Americans frightens people.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepy means giving a feeling of horror or unease.

clue.text: Two-toned bird like a coot?

parts.note: pie is an old name for the magpie
the phrase 'bald as a coot' refers to the bird's white forehead patch

explanation.surface: A two-coloured bird is said to resemble a coot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' looks like the definition for a coot-like creature; the definition is the adjective at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Piebald describes an animal patched in two colours, usually black and white.

clue.text: In court, quote strange European trifler

indicators.note: in places the scrambled word inside the court letters
strange means odd, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd European is quoted in court as a flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges only the word quote, and 'In' puts that inside the court abbreviation; the European letter is added at the very end, outside the court.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquette is a flirt, someone who trifles with others' affections.

clue.text: Kit's regular strip

definitions.meaning: kit is a set of clothing worn by a team, the 's standing for is
regular means even and unvarying, the same throughout
a football strip is the outfit a team plays in

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a set of clothing, the adjective for unvarying, and a sports team's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniform is a team's kit or strip, and as an adjective it means regular or unvarying.

clue.text: Not firm? Insert nail possibly to hold it up

annotationWithheld.clue: Not firm? Insert nail possibly to hold it up

clue.text: French courses, nothing too saucy?

parts.note: reads as French lessons kept free of anything risque, but describes a lighter style of French cookery that avoids rich sauces

explanation.surface: A language school promises French classes with nothing racy in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' means meal courses, not lessons, and 'saucy' is literal: the style cut back the heavy sauces of classic French cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1970s style of French cookery served light, small dishes without heavy sauces.

clue.text: Some will be attached to board to do the filing

definitions.text: Some will be attached to board to do the filing

parts.words: Some will be attached to board to do the filing
parts.note: reads as staff joining a company board to handle the paperwork, but describes an abrasive stuck to a strip of card for filing fingernails

explanation.surface: Some new staff will join the company board to deal with the filing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' and 'filing' suggest an office; they mean a nail board and smoothing nails.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is the gritty abrasive coating an emery board, used to file fingernails.

clue.text: Points to Bill in aircraft's front

parts.note: E for east is a compass point
S for south is another compass point

indicators.note: in places the word for bill inside the word for aircraft

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft
a bill is a poster or advert, so ad

explanation.surface: Someone directs a bill to the front of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' looks like the front of the plane, but the definition is a seafront, the British word for a seaside promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level promenade along a seafront, often simply called the front in Britain.

clue.text: Small animal with a small butterfly

indicators.note: with signals that the answer joined to a gives the butterfly, so a is taken away from it

parts.note: a pupa is the chrysalis stage of a butterfly, playfully called a small one

explanation.surface: A tiny creature keeps company with a little butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer with A added makes PUPA, the chrysalis stage, so the wordplay is PUPA without its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A pup is a young animal such as a baby dog or seal.

clue.text: Chemical giving neat skin to Cockney

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

indicators.note: Cockneys famously drop the h at the start of words, so it is removed

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin

explanation.surface: A tidy skin-care product is offered to a Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like an adjective but is an old noun for cattle. A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner, whose accent drops H.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with another element.

clue.text: In the end Gulliver departs without a good word for Swift

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around the next pieces
only the final letter of the name is taken

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for departs in timetables
pi is short for pious, meaning good

explanation.surface: Gulliver finally leaves without a kind word for Jonathan Swift, who wrote his travels.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift is the author of Gulliver's Travels, a neat misdirection: here it means fast. 'without' means outside, so R and D enclose A PI.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift and the answer are synonyms meaning fast or quick.

clue.text: The Sultanate's extremely cloudy divination

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: The sultanate's weather forecast is mostly overcast, read as a kind of fortune-telling.
explanation.definitionFit: Theomancy is divination by oracles or by people believed inspired by a god.
